name: SeaweedFS
description: S3-compatible object storage in one container. Buckets and objects over a signed S3 API — a target for Panelica's remote backups, for application uploads, or for anything that speaks S3.

ports.description: Master status page. It has no login, so it stays on localhost; reach it with an SSH tunnel.
Filer: file browser and plain HTTP access to the same data. No login either, so localhost only.

env_vars.description: Access key id your S3 clients use
Secret access key (auto-generated). It is the only credential the API accepts — keep a copy.
Size a storage volume reaches before the master starts a new one. 1 GB suits a single server; raise it for large data sets.

volumes.description: Buckets, objects and the filer's metadata

command:
set -e
mkdir -p /data
# One S3 identity, from the credentials the panel generated. Without a
# config file SeaweedFS answers every unsigned request, so this file is
# what keeps the endpoint closed.
cat > /data/.s3-identities.json <<JSON
{"identities":[{"name":"$S3_ACCESS_KEY","credentials":[{"accessKey":"$S3_ACCESS_KEY","secretKey":"$S3_SECRET_KEY"}],"actions":["Admin","Read","Write","List","Tagging"]}]}
JSON
chmod 600 /data/.s3-identities.json
exec weed server -dir=/data -ip=localhost -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 -master.volumeSizeLimitMB="$VOLUME_SIZE_LIMIT_MB" -volume.max=0 -master.raftHashicorp -master.electionTimeout=1s -filer -s3 -s3.port=8333 -s3.config=/data/.s3-identities.json -s3.port.iceberg=0 -s3.port.lance=0
post_install_notes:
The S3 endpoint is http://<server>:8333 and it only answers signed requests — the access key and secret are on the credentials card. Create your first bucket with any S3 client, for example `aws --endpoint-url http://<server>:8333 s3 mb s3://backups`, or point Panelica's remote backup at it (S3-compatible, path-style, region us-east-1).

The master and filer pages carry no login, so they are published on 127.0.0.1 only; reach them over an SSH tunnel (`ssh -L 9333:127.0.0.1:9333 ...`) when you want to look at volumes or browse files.

After a restart the S3 API answers for about six seconds with InternalError while the master elects itself; retry and it is there. Nothing is lost - buckets and objects are on the volume.

Everything lives on the data volume: objects, buckets and the filer's metadata. The secret key is written into /data/.s3-identities.json at every start from the environment, so changing the variable and restarting the container rotates it.

credential_patterns.label: Region / addressing
credential_patterns.value: us-east-1, path-style (set 'force path style' in your client)

credential_patterns.label: Master & filer
credential_patterns.value: http://127.0.0.1:9333 and http://127.0.0.1:8888 — localhost only, no login
